instruction: Export the LibreOffice Impress file to PNG format and save it as final.png on the Desktop. Use the default export configuration.

metadata.explanation: Validates PNG export has minimum total pixels (320,000) and aspect ratio between 1.5-1.9 (close to 16:9). Ensures proper export quality. Verified: 320k pixels = ~800x400, reasonable for default export.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator cannot verify the PNG was actually exported from LibreOffice Impress - it only checks if ANY PNG file exists with the correct filename and resolution
No content verification: Cannot distinguish between a properly exported presentation slide vs a renamed/downloaded/screenshot PNG file
No source verification: The evaluator would pass even if the user simply renamed an existing PNG to 'final.png' without performing the export operation
Missing verification of 'default export configuration' requirement - cannot verify export settings were used
Getter and metric logic are correct for what they do (check file existence and resolution), but semantically insufficient to verify the instruction was completed as intended
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Add metadata verification: Check PNG metadata (e.g., creator software field) to confirm it was generated by LibreOffice
Add visual content verification: Use OCR or image comparison to verify the PNG contains content from the source PPTX file
Add temporal verification: Check file creation timestamp to ensure it was created after the task started (though this could be spoofed)
Consider using accessibility tree or LibreOffice state to verify the export dialog was actually used
Alternative: Simplify instruction to 'Verify a PNG file named final.png exists on Desktop with reasonable presentation dimensions' to match what the evaluator actually checks
